rules.summary: A ProtocolVersion must expose commitment_points.
Each CommitmentPoint must include Authority, Evidence, Reasoning, Dependency, Version, and Recourse gates.
Each CommitmentPoint must state the basis for its binding or non-binding effect.
Advisory-looking commitment points require analysis showing whether they indirectly bind downstream action.
A commitment point that can produce an adverse outcome must declare a recourse_state.
Canonical protocol data cannot contain runtime connector, credential, worker, endpoint, retry, timeout, or UI bindings.
Task ownership is not legal authority unless delegation or authority holder is declared.
Evidence gates must not rely only on derived runtime state.
AI or probabilistic model output cannot be deterministic gate authority.
Temporal evaluation requires explicit current_time.
CommitmentPoint dependencies must resolve to known commitment points or declared external references.
Version gates that require protocol version pinning must declare protocol_version_id.
Conformance claims must identify subject, class, ICSL version, test-suite version, and result.
Conformance class must be one of the candidate ICSL conformance classes.
Conformance result must be one of pass, fail, not_run, or partial.
Receipts must form a valid previous_hash chain and any declared content_hash must match canonical content.
A Corpus-L3 package cannot leave recourse as unknown_unpublished where adverse outcomes exist.
Binding force and procedural outcome semantics must be explicit where a protocol claims execution effect.
Mixed binding force must enumerate its binding-force components.
Recourse state must be one of the ICSL candidate recourse-state enum values.
High-fidelity or public-impact adverse commitments must include governance addendum fields.
Governance addendum must include notice, participation, discretion, remedy, oversight, and reason-giving fields.
Labels, explanations, and UI text cannot alter gate evaluation unless mapped into canonical semantics.
Normative references must declare version, date, or stable retrieval basis.
Human renderings cannot introduce semantics absent from canonical protocol data.
Unsupported extended features must be rejected or downgraded according to declared conformance class.
An ICSL package must include a package manifest.
Package hash vectors must match declared package files.
Every file declared in the package manifest must exist in the package.
Hash vectors must cover every non-hash-vector file declared by the package manifest.
